articles.summary_snippet: In a world carved into continental blocs by authoritarians, Britain has to make common cause with its neighbours In the chronicles of 21st-century diplomacy few statements have caused as much offence with as few words as Barack Obama’s 2014 description of Russia as a “regional power” . Vladimir Putin’s politics were defined then, as now, by vengeful resentment of his country’s relegation from superpower status after the cold war. His worldview is warped by a paranoid conviction that Nato never stopped striving to deepen that humiliation, even after the USSR had unravelled. From his Kremlin throne, the Russian president expects to be treated as a colossus of world history. It is hard to overstate how bitterly he hated being dismissed by Obama as a geopolitical B-lister. articles.title: How Ukraine struck the Kerch bridge, a symbol of Putin’s rule
articles.summary_snippet: With the SpaceX satellite system faltering, Ukraine’s military launched a surprise, multi-pronged attack to take down vital bridge to Crimea At 10pm on Monday evening a Ukrainian soldier scrawled a message on a kamikaze drone. It said simply: “The bridge is fucked.” He then added: “We will stand and Moscow will fall.” It was a freezing night, with a bright starry sky and no clouds. Lines of ice had formed on the drone’s bulky wings. Soon, it would be hurtling towards its target – about 500km to the south. Typically the soldiers who gathered in this muddy field in central Ukraine were attacking oil refineries deep inside Russia. In recent months the work had become almost mundane: they had hit so many of them. The objective that evening, however, was unique. articles.summary_snippet: This month, the league rightly honors veterans across the US. But little is mentioned about the death tolls, or the reasons behind our wars My mom taught me to thank veterans. Whenever we saw someone in a veterans hat, she set the example. Nobody in her family served, but my paternal grandfather fought in the Pacific in the second world war, and she was always grateful to hear his stories, even the repeats. It’s one of the things she gave me that I held on to, even in my worst years. The anger I’ve carried about the unjust wars of my lifetime – Afghanistan, Iraq and now Iran – never targeted the people sent to fight them. Continue reading...

It is no irony to Trump that he has elevated Miller as his ideal bullying enforcer only after Trump’s own thorough repudiation. Appointing Miller is Trump’s denial that he is the worst thing he could possibly imagine: a loser. Trump has no more time for adults in the room who might want to negotiate with the new powers-that-be in the Congress. He has searched his soul, as he explained in his interview on 60 Minutes , entertaining his wish to ascend to heaven. Continue reading...

articles.summary_snippet: Guatemala Profile Guatemala's criminal organizations are among the most sophisticated and dangerous in Central America. Some of them have been in operation for decades. They include former members of the military, intelligence agencies and active members of the police. Transporting illegal drugs north comprises the bulk of their activity, but organized crime in Guatemala is also involved in marijuana and poppy cultivation, as well as human trafficking, kidnapping, extortion, money laundering, arms smuggling, adoption rings, eco trafficking and other illegal enterprises. They often work with groups from Mexico, Colombia and other Central American nations and they have the potential to expand and command other Central American nations' underworlds. The tornado reached 160 metres wide, had a path length of 4.4 miles (7.1km) and reached estimated peak winds of up to 100mph (161km/h). There were no injuries or fatalities but windows and roofs were damaged on several homes, a large hotel sign fell on to a number of cars, and a semi truck overturned on I95. Although Delaware often experiences a few tornadoes every year, this is only the second time the state has had tornado activity in November since 1950, according to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration.
